note: Backtest of the fair-value rule on Wallex 1-minute last-trade candles, 2026-09-22T07:00 to 2026-10-22T07:00 UTC (30 days), markets POLTMN, SANDTMN. Fair value = Binance 1m close x Wallex USDTTMN close; entry when the modelled ask is at least 0.70% (toman) below fair value after the market's 180-minute median baseline, skipped when Binance fell more than 0.4% in that minute; exits as the live engine: target when sell_dev >= -0.05% AND the bid clears both taker fees + 0.05%, stop -0.9%, time 25 min; net = (1 - taker)^2 x bid / ask - 1. Wallex history has no order book: fills are modelled at the signal minute's close +/- half the measured median spread (research/live_spreads_watch.json). Overall 0 trades, mean n/a per trade, win None%, sum +0.00 percentage points. Caveats: most signals are single-minute last-trade prints that are gone by the next traded minute; entering one traded minute later (same rule, next traded minute's close) turns the mean to n/a per trade over 0 trades. The live engine polls the real order book every 2.5 s, so only a real ask that far below fair counts. 0 of the 0 trades came when Wallex USDTTMN had not traded for over 5 minutes (mostly at night, about 20:00 to 05:30 UTC in this data), so their fair value uses a stale USDT/TMN price; their mean is n/a against n/a for the rest. Each market's row carries the same checks for that market: next_minute_mean_ret_pct (entry one traded minute later) and stale_usdt_trades / stale_usdt_mean_ret_pct; read mean_ret_pct only together with next_minute_mean_ret_pct. Treat these numbers as an optimistic upper bound, not a forecast; markets with few trades say little.
